note: Coordinates locate modern sites, city centres or general historical localities on the present-day OpenStreetMap basemap. Historical boundaries, individual camp positions and itineraries are not being asserted by city-point pins. Badr battlefield and Uhud landmark coordinates are contemporary mapped localities. Historical locations such as Hudaybiyyah are mentioned contextually and omitted from precise pins where coordinates are uncertain.
basemap: © OpenStreetMap contributors. Tiles are a modern reference map, not a reconstructed seventh-century landscape.

groups.description: The sanctuary, migration, battles, neighbouring frontiers and the first community

groups.name: Imperial and scholarly centres
groups.description: Major cities of early Islamic rule and later Mediterranean intellectual history

groups.name: Trade and wider communities

entries.name: Makkah
entries.context: Sanctuary, early revelation, Meccan opposition, the truce's destination and the eventual return.

entries.name: Madinah (Yathrib)
entries.context: Place of the Hijrah and the integration of worship, household responsibilities and public obligations.

entries.name: Ṭāʾif
entries.context: City associated with the Prophet's search for receptive hearers and with the later campaign and siege.

entries.name: Badr
entries.context: The town and battlefield locality southwest of Madinah; exact early troop positions require separate critical reconstruction.

entries.name: Mount Uḥud
entries.context: Mountain north of Madinah, where the 625 CE battle and burial of martyrs are associated with this landscape.

entries.name: Khaybar
entries.context: Oasis north of Madinah, linked to reported cultivation agreements and the setting of ʿUmar's land endowment.

entries.name: Tabūk
entries.context: Northern Arabian location associated with an expedition during the last years of the Prophet's life.

entries.name: Najrān
entries.context: South Arabian religious and frontier context where communities interacted with Red Sea and Arabian powers.

entries.name: Aksum
entries.context: Royal centre of a Christian kingdom that offered refuge to early Muslim emigrants.

entries.name: Jerusalem
entries.context: Religious centre central to the Night Journey and to later Islamic, Christian and Jewish political histories.

entries.name: Damascus
entries.context: Syrian provincial and later Umayyad centre within the history of public authority and scholarship.

entries.name: Baghdad
entries.context: Abbasid capital with major traditions of administration, translation, medicine and learned argument.

entries.name: Kūfah
entries.context: Iraqi garrison town and scholarly setting important to early juristic reasoning and political contest.

entries.name: Baṣrah
entries.context: Iraqi garrison and trading city, with important textual, legal and intellectual schools.

entries.name: Cairo
entries.context: Later urban centre of scholarship, power and pilgrimage networks.

entries.name: Córdoba
entries.context: Major Andalusian political, intellectual and artistic city.

entries.name: Granada
entries.context: Andalusian centre associated with the final Nasrid emirate and the events of 1492.

entries.name: Fes
entries.context: Maghribi city with a long history of scholarly learning, craftsmanship and public life.

entries.name: Timbuktu
entries.context: Middle Niger centre of manuscript culture, trade, Muslim scholarship and changing political authority.

entries.name: Gao
entries.context: A Niger River centre in the political and commercial history of the Songhay world.

entries.name: Surat
entries.context: Indian Ocean commercial centre involved in maritime finance, pilgrimage and diverse mercantile networks.

entries.name: Melaka
entries.context: Malay port where political authority, shipping, multilingual exchange and Muslim communities interacted.

entries.name: Bagerhat
entries.context: Historic Bengali settlement and mosque complex associated with canals, religious patronage and cultivation.

entries.name: Sylhet
entries.context: Bengal city associated with the family endowment whose validity reached the Privy Council in 1894.

entries.name: Delhi
entries.context: Political and educational centre of South Asian Muslim history, including Mughal and colonial transitions.

entries.name: Lahore
entries.context: Persianate and South Asian scholarly and administrative city within changing imperial worlds.
